entities.name: Predator Hound
entities.description:
The Predator Hound, also known as a Predadog, is a non-sapient species used by the Upgrade Predator to hunt and chase down and kill prey.

A pair of Predator Hounds were brought to Earth during the Upgrade Predator's pursuit of the Fugitive Predator. The Loonies managed to kill one whereas the other was pacified due to head trauma, acting much like a regular dog. The surviving hound assisted the Loonies by handing them grenades and even turning against its own master.

Predator Hounds are chimeric canines created through hybridization techniques similar to ones used to augment their master with base genome being an unspecified extraterrestrial hound species. Yautja DNA is among addition genomes involved in their creation through their jarring resemblance to the race donor in question, most notable being tanned hide, green blood, and dreadlocks on their head, though the Hounds lacked mandibles. Like Upgrade Predator himself, they possess exo-skeletal armor that can deflect bullets and wrist blades that make forceful contact on it, though still pale in comparison to the former's as they can still be injured with point-blank shot. Yet, Predator Hounds's internal organs seemed much softer and susceptible to damage than the rest, as Quinn managed to kill one by firing several grenade rounds into its throat, causing it to explode from inside out.

Superficially, Predator Hounds are very similar to the Hell-Hounds used by the Super Predators and even deployed for the same function. Even so, Predator Hounds seem to be better suited for tracking and retrieval tasks as two of them were deployed by Upgrade Predator to locate and secure Fugitive Predator's equipment that already delivered to Rory.

entities.name: Proto-Xenomorph XX033
entities.description:
Proto–Xenomorph XX033, also dubbed the Proto–Xenomorph or Protomorph, was a species of endoparasitoid creature bearing similarities to Xenomorph XX121. Stages of the Proto–Xenomorph life cycle included the Trilobite and the Deacon. Proto–Xenomorphs were spawned by living Proto-Hives, which were in turn created by the beings known as the Fulfremmen.

Ionic proto–plasmamorphs, otherwise known as the Hessdalen Lights, were the first stage in the Proto–Xenomorph life cycle. Essentially mobile spores, they would attach to a station or ship and begin its transformation into a Proto-Hive.

The Utero–Pod was the next stage in the Proto–Xenomorph life cycle. As it gained a foothold in the structure to which it was attached, the Proto–Hive would sabotage life support systems and secure hosts in a centralized chamber. There, the hosts were suspended from the ceiling of the chamber and injected with genetic material from Heptopus tabellarium; the process began their transformation into proto–Ovomorphic Utero–Pods. The pods, also dubbed "Womb–Bats", would eventually disgorge Naiads.

In the case that no Womb–Bats were available, Heptopus tabellarium would take the form of a single–celled organism dubbed the Xygote or "eye–worm". The Xygote could be transferred by way of tears, saliva, or blood, and would then implant itself in the abdominal cavity of its host. Regardless of the host's gender, the resultant embryo would grow into a fetus, sapping the victim's strength as it leached biological material to supply its own development. It would then forcibly emerge as a Naiad, killing the host.

entities.description:
right|thumb|210px|The Ceremonial Mask made from the Quatza-Rij. The Quatza-Rij is a creature native to Yautja Prime, the homeworld of the . They are known as one of the fiercest creatures indigenous to Yautja Prime.

As a tradition, young Yautja hunters always hunt in groups of three. They are sent out in packs and must kill a single Quatza-Rij as a team in order to be recognized as adult clan members. Only after years of hunting, do the most skilled and experienced Yautja try to kill a Quatza-Rij on their own. If successful, they can break away from their pack and are allowed to travel off-world to hunt bigger game.

The Ceremonial mask is worn by the elder Predators during the "rite of passage" ceremony of the young hunters. It's fashioned from the skin and bone of one of the Quatza-Rij.

The Ceremonial mask has no laser sight, as it's not a hunting helmet, but is decorated with three circles on the forehead which represents each of the three hunters. The symbol of unity and teamwork, the Yautja laser sight is modeled after this symbol.

Around the size of a large dog, this creature possessed both avian and basal reptile traits, with a large head that resembled Earthen birds of prey and a featherless body which ended in a pair of twin barbed tails. Their beak-like mouths were lined with long sharp teeth, and their heads sat upon a long flexible neck.

They were stronger than an adult human man, capable of tearing off parts of limbs with a simple twist of their large heads. Much like a Komodo dragon, they employed mobbing tactics and would eat their prey alive.

They were incredibly agile, which made them hard to shoot, should someone have to defend themselves from the creatures.

entities.name: Rhynth
entities.description:
Rhynths, also known as a poke-snoots, are large cattle-like quadrupedal ungulates that bear a striking resemblance to an Earth rhinoceros.

These large herbivores look strikingly similar to Earth rhinos, except their two horns are side by side, not one in front of the other, and they also have a long, thick tail. They have a large skeleton and a thick tan-colored hide that can be made into leather, and this hide can be either uniform in coloration or covered in large splotches, like that of an Earth cow, though they are purple in coloration. This coloration may indicate different varieties or possibly gender. They appear to lack hair, though it is possible that it is only sparse, seeing as they are native to an extremely arid world.

It is noticeable that all rhynth have similarly-sized horns, which may indicate that they are used for protection against such predators like briar wolves. It does not seem likely that the horns are used for competition with one another, especially since young ones also possess well-developed horns. Their mitochondrial cell count is significantly lower than most found in their quadrant.

Though this species may appear to be mammalian, seeing as they resemble rhinos and are raised like cows, it is possible that they are reptilian, as there are several aspects that are more often found in reptiles, such as their tails, though this is only speculation.

entities.name: River Ghost
entities.description:
The "River Ghosts" are extraterrestrial creatures that are humanoid in appearance, but are shrouded in pale, insect-like exoskeletons that cover almost all of their bodies. While they have recesses comparable to human eye sockets on the front of their head, they do not appear to possess any visible eyes, while a sensory organ covered by a moveable flap of bone is located in the center of their forehead. Their teeth extend forwards from their mouth on plates of bone, leaving a considerable gap to their mouths. They have greatly elongated talons on their hands, and strange, bony, almost wing-like protrusions on their back.

The River Ghosts appear to have some form of symbiotic relationship with small insectoid organisms that live on their skin. The exact purpose of these small creatures is unknown, although it is possible they help to keep the River Ghosts' skin clean from bacteria and other potentially infections parasites, similar to many Earth-based symbiotes. Aside from possessing intelligence, they're also faster, more agile and more deadly than humans. One of their kind managed to avoid the traps set by Royce's team and nearly catches Edwin in a chase before it was shot by Noland.

Like humans, River Ghosts were 'dropped' on the Game Preserve Planet to be hunted by the Super Predators for sport. This suggests that the River Ghosts were somehow worthy prey for the Super Predators, possibly because of their speed. One such creature was encountered by Royce and the other humans dropped with him on the Game Preserve Planet in 2010. The creature attacked the group and pursued Edwin, presumably intending to kill him, before it was shot dead by Noland.

The River Ghost's role was reduced in the final film, compared to earlier drafts: it was originally supposed to play a more substantial part in the film, stalking the characters for longer and leading them to believe it was the one responsible for their being on the planet. In another draft of the script, the creature was originally to have been found near a river and was barely seen, behaving almost like a ghost or apparition (it was from this draft that the creature earned its moniker).

These five-meter-high birds stood can be found in groups and use their hooked beaks and long, purple, barbed tongues to strip limbs from trees and trample them beneath their massive, taloned feet. The tall and muscular creatures have a thick coat of moss-green feathers. They also have an impressive bone crest that runs from the top of their skull, between the eyes, and curves around their beak-like armor.

They’re not predators, but they’re still dangerous and could take down a security fence. When threatened, Shovel-heads will clumped together in a circle, ready to strike at attackers to defend themselves. If given the opportunity to escape, Shevels will let out a bellowing call and charged away from attackers, not attempting to dodge anything, just lowering their heads and bowling right through trees, bushes, and any animals unfortunate enough to be in the way.

Shovel-heads are similar to, but much larger than, an Australian [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassowary cassowary].

The snuffle–squirrel was a small herbivore native to the planet Zagreus. Similar to the squirrel of Earth, the snuffle–squirrel was ubiquitous throughout Zagreus' biosphere and featured a number of distinguishing traits.

The evolutionary equivalent to an Earth squirrel, the snuffle-squirrel was a long-bodied, low-slung creature with four eyes and green fur. It possessed four front-mounted caterpillar legs and four more at its rear, and waving pom-pom-like cilia along the length of its body that enabled it to properly navigate, hunt, climb, and forage. Juveniles were distinguished by a thin tail and spiked fur. The snuffle–squirrel was predated upon by the lion-worm.

entities.name: Tanaka 5 Scorpion
entities.description:
The Tanaka 5 Scorpion is a relatively large species of arthropod-like aliens native to the planet Tanaka 5. They bear quite a striking resemblance to the scorpions of Earth.

As their name would suggest, they are quite similar in appearance to scorpions, possessing a long stinger-tipped tail and a pair of claws. However, these features differ from those of an actual scorpion. Their tails are quite articulate compared to that of actual scorpions, the stinger also appears to point down instead of up.

The fact that the tail and stinger are quite thin and small, along with the large claws (chelae) that they possess, suggests the scorpions possess weak venom and instead rely on their claws to crush prey, rarely using their stinger. The pedipalps that the claws are attached to appear to have some form of armor on the "shoulder".

They possess yellowish blood. It is unknown what their mouth looks like or how many eyes they possess.

entities.name: Tanakan Scorpionid
entities.description:
The Tanakan Scorpionid is a huge arthropod native to the planet Tanaka 5.

Having more in common with Earth's prehistoric sea scorpions than actual scorpions, the Tanakan Scorpionid possesses a rounded head, a set of large pincers, eight crab-like legs, two large fin-like structures on either side of their bodies and stinger tail filled with deadly venom. Their shells can protect them from melee attacks but are pretty weak against ballistic damage, their pincers are strong enough to break a man’s leg, their fins first thought to be utilized in intimidation display make them actually excellent swimmers and their sting can kill a grown human quickly unless an antidote is administered.

The Tanakan Scorpionids are nocturnal creatures, they usually live either in the desert or the planet's cavernous springs. They hide in dunes and rocks during the day and usually hunts at night either on ground or water. The scorpionids are a pretty timid creature and won't fight unless there's a good reason however if provoked they'll aggressively attack whatever threatens them using mainly their claws and stinger.

The Tanakan Scorpionids are hunted for their venom used for a multitude of medicinal purposes

entities.name: Tentacle
entities.description:
The Tentacle is an animal native to LV-1201.

Tentacles are worm-like subterranean predators with a beige, reptilian hide. Its has no jaws, instead possessing a round mouth lined by a rozette of backwards-facing teeth. It also has rudimentary eyes, suggesting its ancestors lived above ground. Tentacles hunt in packs, attacking their prey from below the ground like a terrestrial version of the crocodile. When attacking, they can rise up to two meters into the air.

Both Dunya and the Ancient Predator encounter these organisms on LV-1201. They are very easy to kill depending on difficulty level.

entities.name: Tetrabrachial Humanoids
entities.description:
The Tetrabrachial Humanoids are an otherwise unnamed species native to the planet UE-753.

The humanoids were native to UE-753 in the Kaus Borealis System, and appeared to be living in a human equivalent of a bronze age, while still maintaining a tribal air. They have reddish skin, emotive faces, four arms with three-fingered hands, and speak their own language. Physically, they seem to be on par with the in terms of strength, though their technology was still primitive and infinitely inferior.

The humanoids possessed cave paintings of Engineers, very similar to those seen on Earth during Doctor Elizabeth Shaw's expedition in Isle of Skye, suggesting that the latter species may have been responsible for seeding UE-753 with life.

Roughly during the year 2107, the Yautja Ahab conducted a Hunt within UE-753. Resulting in the deaths of at least three humanoids. He would go on to discover cave paintings depicting the Engineer species. Ahab would subsequently develop an obsession with the Engineers, and dedicate himself to finding and claiming one as a Trophy.

entities.description:
Ticks, also referred to as "Species 19," were a species of alien specimen present aboard the Weyland-Yutani Corporation exploratory vessel as of 2120. The creatures attached to a host and fed on their blood, and were capable of absorbing a fatal amount.

The species resembled large leeches or worms with several appendages. Once they attached to the neck of a host, they would rapidly drain it of all its blood, killing the host. During this process, they would become engorged.

Chibuzo, the science officer of the Maginot, noted that while it has a preference for fresh victims, it can feed off of dead tissue if hungry enough.

These creatures hold some measure of intelligence, as it understood how to unscrew the lid of its container to free itself.

entities.name: Tiger
entities.description:
The tiger (Panthera tigris) is a large cat and a member of the genus Panthera native to Asia. It has a powerful, muscular body with a large head and paws, a long tail and orange fur that fades to white in parts, with black, mostly vertical stripes. It is traditionally classified into nine subspecies, though some recognise only two subspecies, the mainland Asian tiger and the Sunda Islands tiger.

Throughout its range, it inhabits mainly forests, from coniferous and temperate broadleaf and mixed forests in the Russian Far East and Northeast China to tropical and subtropical moist broadleaf forests on the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia. The tiger is an apex predator and preys mainly on hooved mammals, which it takes by ambush. It lives a mostly solitary life and occupies home ranges, defending these from individuals of the same sex. The range of a male tiger overlaps with that of multiple females with whom he mates. Females give birth to usually two or three cubs that stay with their mother for about two years. When becoming independent, they leave their mother's home range and establish their own.

Since the early 20th century, tiger populations have lost at least 93% of their historic range and are locally extinct in West and Central Asia, in large areas of China and on the islands of Java and Bali. Today, the tiger's range is severely fragmented. It is listed as Endangered on the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species, as its range is thought to have declined by 53% to 68% since the late 1990s. Major threats to tigers are habitat destruction and fragmentation due to deforestation, poaching for fur and the illegal trade of body parts for medicinal purposes. Tigers are also victims of human–wildlife conflict as they attack and prey on livestock in areas where natural prey is scarce. The tiger is legally protected in all range countries. National conservation measures consist of action plans, anti-poaching patrols and schemes for monitoring tiger populations. In several range countries, wildlife corridors have been established and tiger reintroduction is planned.

The tiger is among the most popular of the world's charismatic megafauna. It has been kept in captivity since ancient times and has been trained to perform in circuses and other entertainment shows. The tiger featured prominently in the ancient mythology and folklore of cultures throughout its historic range and has continued to appear in culture worldwide.

entities.name: Trypanohyncha Ocellus
entities.description:
The Ocellus was a small creature that is essentially an eyeball with tentacles protruding from underneath it. The eye was able to alter itself to change the number of pupils it possessed; it is able to control living and dead hosts.

Its description on various screens from the laboratory of the USCSS Maginot stated the following:

A smooth scoleum features several ocular irises and a tentacle system that can grow or retract at will. The tentacles carry extraordinary strength and are built to climb into and dislodge the eyes of other living organisms. Once replaced in the eye socket, T. Ocellus takes over the ocular pathways to the brain, overriding the neurotransmissions throughout the body. More study is needed to gauge imminent intelligence, though T. Ocellus has shown remarkable problem-solving skills at near-human measure.

During study within the Neverland facility, it was revealed that control of an organic being was near instantaneous once implanted.

entities.name: Tuber
entities.description:
Tubers are a type of enlarged structure that plants use as storage organs for nutrients, derived from stems or roots. Tubers help plants perennate (survive winter or dry months), provide energy and nutrients, and are a means of asexual reproduction.

Stem tubers manifest as thickened rhizomes (underground stems) or stolons (horizontal connections between organisms); examples include the potato and yam. The term root tuber describes modified lateral roots, as in sweet potato, cassava, and dahlia.

This species shares many characteristics with frogs on planet Earth. Except that it has two enormous, pupil-less, bulbous yellow eyes, only two hind legs, and a tail. It is also capable of croaking.

During the year 2041, Theta Berwick was studying and cataloging this species in her notebook, until she was called by her parents.

Theta tried several names for this species: Damara Anura, Damara Lithobates Virids Cauda and Damara Green Long-Tail Frog.

entities.name: Wild boar
entities.description:
Wild boars, known taxonomically as Sus scrofa, are a group of suid animals native to Earth. As of 1990, up to 16 subspecies are recognized, which are divided into four regional groupings. Human intervention has spread its distribution further, making the species one of the widest-ranging mammals in the world.

The wild boar is a bulky, massively built suid with short and relatively thin legs. The trunk is short and massive, while the hindquarters are comparatively underdeveloped. The region behind the shoulder blades rises into a hump and the neck is short and thick to the point of being nearly immobile. The animal's head is very large, taking up to one-third of the body's entire length. The structure of the head is well suited for digging. The head acts as a plough, while the powerful neck muscles allow the animal to upturn considerable amounts of soil: it is capable of digging 8–10 cm (3.1–3.9 in) into frozen ground and can upturn rocks weighing 40–50 kg (88–110 lb). The eyes are small and deep-set and the ears long and broad. The species has well developed canine teeth, which protrude from the mouths of adult males. The middle hooves are larger and more elongated than the lateral ones and are capable of quick movements. The animal can run at a maximum speed of 40 km/h and jump at a height of 140–150 cm (55–59 in).

Boars are typically social animals, living in female-dominated sounders consisting of barren sows and mothers with young led by an old matriarch. Male boars leave their sounder at the age of 8–15 months, while females either remain with their mothers or establish new territories nearby. Subadult males may live in loosely knit groups, while adult and elderly males tend to be solitary outside the breeding season.

The wild boar features prominently in the cultures of people, many of which saw the animal as embodying warrior virtues. Cultures throughout Europe and Asia Minor saw the killing of a boar as proof of one's valor and strength.

The Xenomorphs were vicious predatory creatures with no higher goals than the propagation of their species and the destruction of any life that could pose a threat to them. Like wasps, bees, or ants, Xenomorphs were eusocial, with a fertile Queen breeding a host of subordinate castes. The creatures were known for their potent acidic blood and their pharyngeal jaws, although their biological life cycle, in which their offspring are implanted inside living hosts before erupting violently from their chests, was in many ways their signature aspect.

Aside from their repeated conflicts with humans, Xenomorphs were often associated with the , who know them as kainde amedha ("hard meat"). The Yautja revered the creatures as incredibly dangerous and thus highly worthy prey, notably employing them in initiation Hunts that serve to test young members of their society and mark their progression into adulthood.

Xenomorphs were primarily solitary ambush predators, although they were known to adopt swarm tactics when acting in larger groups. Despite their voracious ability to kill, they often sought to take their victims alive to be hosts for more Xenomorphs; victims were taken to a Hive (or simply a secluded location if no Hive existed), cocooned and/or immobilized before being impregnated with a Xenomorph embryo. However, when their target became a threat or was deemed unsuitable for harvest, the Xenomorph would not hesitate to quickly dispatch the chosen host.

If Xenomorphs established a presence on a world, it was exceedingly difficult to root them out. Any such planet or moon effectively became useless to humans due to the threat the creatures posed to terrestrial operations.

entities.name: Yautja
entities.description:
The Yautja, (pronounced Ya-OOT-ja or YOWT-ja), known colloquially as the Predators or Hunters, are an extraterrestrial species characterized by their hunting of other dangerous species for sport and honor, including humans. The Yautja are a sentient humanoid race that breathe an atmosphere similar to that of Earth's but possess a level of technological advancement far in excess of anything available to humans. The Predators stalk and kill their prey using a combination of highly advanced technology, such as active camouflage and energy weapons, combined with comparatively primitive traditional weapons, such as blades, spears and nets. The Predators often ritualistically mutilate their prey and usually claim a trophy from their kills. Capable of interstellar travel in star ships, the Predators have hunted on Earth for centuries and have also had prior contact with the Engineers.

Aside from their repeated conflicts with humans, the Predators have notably been associated with Xenomorph XX121, known to them as kainde amedha ("hard meat"), whom they revere as perhaps the worthiest of all prey. They have been known to deliberately breed the creatures from captive Queens in order to hunt them, often as part of initiation rituals for young Predators.

Predators are bipedal humanoids, physically distinguishable from humans by their greater height, the long, hair-like appendages on their heads (nicknamed dreadlocks), clawed hands, reptilian skin and their faces, which feature arthropod-like mandibles and no visible nose. The biological purpose of the distinctive mandibles is unclear – some have proposed they may be used in reproduction or mating rituals. They may also be a vestigial piece of anatomy, as noted by Lex Woods, who compares it to the human appendix. Yautja use them to convey emotions; for example, flared mandibles apparently signify anger or surprise, mandibles clicking together can signify interest or curiosity, and Yautja have even been said to "grin" with them. Predators have also been known to employ their mandibles as weapons, using them to inflict grievous bite wounds on their opponent. As well as the fleshy dreadlocks around the side of the head, some Predators have also been seen to possess sparse quills on their cheeks and above the eyes.

While generally uniform, each Yautja's physical appearance includes a number of subtle variations, akin to human genetic diversity. Similarly, while Predator heights vary, they are typically over 7 feet tall, although some have been known to grow to 8 feet or even taller. Despite this, shorter individuals have been recorded, such as Mahnde or the aptly-named Shorty, who stood the height of a typical human. These individuals are unusual and their smaller height the subject of ridicule in Yautja society. The species' reptile-like skin can range in color from light to dark, be mottled or clear, and can appear dry or moist and clammy.

entities.description:
The "Zeevan gorilla" was a species of large tetrabrachial ape-like animal native to the planet Zeevan. They could be used as hosts by s, producing a type of Gorilla Alien.

These creatures greatly resembled Earth apes like gorillas and orangutans, but notably possessed four arms. They also possessed five bony osteoderms curving down either side of their face from a central bone plate on their forehead, getting smaller with each subsequent osteoderm. Their skin and fur was a purplish color.

The Zeevan gorilla's vocal calls were similar to that Earth gorillas. They lived in large troops and unlike Earth gorillas, they were known to be arboreal, similar to orangutans.

The Omni-Tech Outpost was a colony on the planet Mira Ceti 4, with the hopes of making it habital.

The colony was mostly filled with Omni-Tech staff and pioneers, civilian recruits. Amongst those civilian recruits were a deranged cult known as the Esoteric Brotherhood of Tulitu, the cult frequently caused friction at the outpost due to their habit of refusing to work like the other laborers.

The outpost had a security station, their own security forced and the living quarters, the ventilation system was quite large and spacious, this would prove to be a significant weakness for the colony as this was exploited by the cult to spread the Xenomorph infestation by placing Xenomorph eggs in the vents, allowing the Facehuggers to reach nearly everyone living in the outpost.

Four years later, Omni-Tech assumed the tragedy was due to mass hysteria and moved to try and create another colony on Mira Ceti.

entities.name: Sub-space
entities.description:
Sub-space (a.k.a. hyperspace) was a series of planes

Sub-space was discovered by humans at some point after the reformation of the Weyland-Yutani Corporation. With their discovery, displacement drives (which had already existed for FTL travel) could be used to navigate said planes. Navigating sub-space was more complex than navigating the material universe, to the point that some considered the science to be "eldritch." Transiting from sub-space to real space required a period of deacceleration. Rapid deacceleration could be lethal to a ship's crew.

Sub-space transmission technology existed prior to the 2630s. In the late 27th century, the Thirteen were in the midst of developing technology to use sub-space as a transmission medium, allowing real-time communication across the Human Sphere. Enormous amounts of energy would be required for said communication to function. Weyland-Yutani (or at least the Thirteen) had access to this technology, but reserved it for themselves. Even sending a sub-space transmission not in real time required significant energy expenditure.

Due to the quirks of sub-space transmission, a ghosting effect followed the people who were communicating; an 'echo' of the movements as displayed via hologram. Real-time communication could be enacted at least as far as 500 light years.
